items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: Interviewer mentions Boyce Brown as the aldo player in Chet Roble's band; Interviewee does not mention Boyce Brown or indicate a personal connection.

ctx.x: Well, I certainly hope so. And I think there's a good chance of it, John. I know Gordon's playing, and I admire him enormously, although I resent and envy him. He's going to take my jobs away from me. He's 19. I think he's just turned 20. I don't know. He's going on the road with Muggsy Spanier next Monday, by the way. He adulates Marsala, and I think he has a great deal of the same lightness and deftness about his playing that Marsala showed. There's a sprightliness about Marsala's playing, never mind the tempo…
Is there a... did you ever hear the band that Chet Roble had, which had the same instrumentation as Noon, that is an aldo clarinet and rhythm section? Boyce Brown was the aldo player.
Oh, wait a minute. A trio with Sammy Aaron on bass? No, no, no, no, this is six pieces.
